newsitem.title: USA: Fischer Imaging Q1 revs hurt by OEM revs.
newsitem.headline: Fischer Imaging Q1 revs hurt by OEM revs.

text.p: Fischer Imaging Corp said Tuesday that sharply lower original equipment manufacturer (OEM) revenues brought total revenues down for the first quarter.

"As was the case in the fourth quarter of 1996, the most significant factor in the decline in OEM revenues was lower Tilt-C shipments to GE Medical Systems," it said. "OEM shipments declined more than 50 (percent) as compared to the first quarter of 1997."
The company reported net revenues of $12.3 million for the first quarter against $20.1 million for the same period last year.
Fischer also reported a loss of $0.47 a share compared to a profit of $0.15 for the same period last year.
The company, which makes X-ray imaging systems, said it was experiencing "soft market conditions both internationally as well as in the U.S.," saying the strong dollar was hindering its exports.
"Uncertainties caused by Medicare budget negotiations appear to be delaying capital expenditure decisions at many hospitals," it added.
The company said it was increasing cost cutting measures to bring its manufacturing and other expense levels in line with lower production volumes.
